# sysutils_systemd_dropin (Resource)

Manages a drop-in file that changes the configuration of a systemd unit, `/etc/systemd/system/<unit_name>.d/<name>.conf`, and runs `systemctl daemon-reload` when it changes. The drop-in is given either as text (`content` or `source`) or as attributes: every section is an attribute (`unit`, `service`, `socket`, `scope`, ..., `install`) and every directive of systemd a nested attribute. Requires root privileges and a host booted with systemd.

A drop-in adds to or overrides the settings of a unit without touching its unit file, so it is the way to change units that a package installed: package upgrades replace the unit file in `/usr/lib/systemd/system`, but never a drop-in in `/etc/systemd/system`. It is also the only way to configure scope units, which programs create at runtime and which have no unit files. Use [`sysutils_systemd_unit`](./systemd_unit.md) for units that you define yourself.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Change a unit that a package installed, without replacing its unit file:
# /etc/systemd/system/nginx.service.d/50-limits.conf. nginx is restarted
# when the drop-in changes.
resource "sysutils_systemd_dropin" "nginx_limits" {
  unit_name = "nginx.service"
  name      = "50-limits"

  service = {
    limit_nofile = "65536"
    memory_max   = "1G"
    restart      = "on-failure"
    restart_sec  = "5s"
  }
}

# Replace the command of a unit: an empty assignment first clears the
# vendor's ExecStart=.
resource "sysutils_systemd_dropin" "getty_autologin" {
  unit_name = "getty@tty1.service"
  name      = "autologin"

  service = {
    exec_start = ["", "-/sbin/agetty --autologin admin --noclear %I $TERM"]
  }
}
```

### Scopes, prefixes, unit types and text

```terraform
# Scope units have no unit files; drop-ins are the only way to configure
# them, here the scopes of user sessions started by systemd-logind.
resource "sysutils_systemd_dropin" "session_limits" {
  unit_name = "session-.scope"
  name      = "50-limits"

  scope = {
    runtime_max_sec = "12h"
  }
}

# A drop-in for every service on the host: /etc/systemd/system/service.d.
resource "sysutils_systemd_dropin" "all_services" {
  unit_name = "service"
  name      = "10-timeouts"

  service = {
    timeout_stop_sec = "30s"
  }
}

# A drop-in written as text.
resource "sysutils_systemd_dropin" "ssh_text" {
  unit_name = "ssh.service"
  name      = "override"
  content   = <<-EOT
    [Service]
    Environment=SSHD_OPTS=-o LogLevel=VERBOSE
  EOT
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the drop-in file without the `.conf` suffix, such as `"override"` or `"50-limits"`. systemd applies the drop-ins of a unit in the order of their file names. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `unit_name` (String) The unit that the drop-in configures, including its type suffix, such as `"ssh.service"`. Any unit type is supported, including `.scope` and `.device` units, templates (`"getty@.service"`) and single instances (`"getty@tty1.service"`). A name ending in a dash, such as `"app-.service"`, configures every unit whose name starts with that prefix, and a bare unit type such as `"service"` every unit of the type. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `automount` (Attributes) The `[Automount]` section, see [systemd.automount(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.automount.html). Only for `.automount` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--automount))
- `content` (String) Contents of the drop-in file. Exactly one of `content`, `source` and the section attributes (`unit`, `service`, ..., `install`, `extra_sections`) must be set. When the drop-in is configured with `source` or the section attributes, this reports the file the provider writes, so that the plan shows a diff of the file.
- `extra_sections` (Map of Map of List of String) Further sections, by name, each a map of directive names to lists of values. Use it for custom `X-` sections, which systemd ignores. The sections above have their own attributes and are not allowed here. Sections are written after the others, sorted by name, and their directives sorted by name.
- `install` (Attributes) The `[Install]` section, see [systemd.unit(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.unit.html). Any drop-in may have it. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--install))
- `mount` (Attributes) The `[Mount]` section, see [systemd.mount(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.mount.html). Only for `.mount` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mount))
- `path_section` (Attributes) The `[Path]` section, see [systemd.path(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.path.html). Only for `.path` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--path_section))
- `restart_on_change` (Boolean) Whether to restart the unit (`systemctl try-restart`) when the drop-in changes or is removed and the unit is running, so that the change takes effect. Only applies to single `.service`, `.socket`, `.mount`, `.automount`, `.swap`, `.timer` and `.path` units, not to templates, prefixes or unit types. Changes that systemd does not see, such as comments or formatting, never restart. Defaults to `true`.
- `scope` (Attributes) The `[Scope]` section, see [systemd.scope(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.scope.html). Only for `.scope` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))
- `service` (Attributes) The `[Service]` section, see [systemd.service(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.service.html). Only for `.service` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service))
- `slice` (Attributes) The `[Slice]` section, see [systemd.slice(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.slice.html). Only for `.slice` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slice))
- `socket` (Attributes) The `[Socket]` section, see [systemd.socket(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.socket.html). Only for `.socket` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--socket))
- `source` (String) Path to a local file whose contents are used as the drop-in file. Exactly one of `content`, `source` and the section attributes must be set. Relative paths are resolved against Terraform's working directory; prefer `${path.module}/...`. The source is read during every plan, so a change to its contents plans an update.
- `swap` (Attributes) The `[Swap]` section, see [systemd.swap(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.swap.html). Only for `.swap` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--swap))
- `timeout` (String) Maximum time each `systemctl` invocation may take, as a Go duration such as `"30s"` or `"5m"`. `systemctl try-restart` waits for the unit to restart, so this should exceed the unit's own start and stop timeouts. Defaults to `"2m"`.
- `timer` (Attributes) The `[Timer]` section, see [systemd.timer(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.timer.html). Only for `.timer` units. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timer))
- `unit` (Attributes) The `[Unit]` section, see [systemd.unit(5)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.unit.html). Any drop-in may have it. Every directive is an attribute named in snake case; directives that may be repeated are lists. An empty string writes an empty assignment (`Directive=`), which resets the directive to its default or empties its list. When the drop-in is configured with `content` or `source`, or was imported, the section as read from the file is reported here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--unit))

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) Hex-encoded SHA-256 checksum of the drop-in file. Known at plan time, so other resources can use it to react to changes.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier, `<unit_name>/<name>`.
- `path` (String) Path of the drop-in file, `/etc/systemd/system/<unit_name>.d/<name>.conf`.

- `wants` (List of String) [`Wants=`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.unit.html#Wants=), one line per element.
- `wants_mounts_for` (List of String) [`WantsMountsFor=`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.unit.html#WantsMountsFor=), one line per element. Requires systemd 256 or later.

## Drop-ins as Attributes

The section and directive attributes are the same as those of [`sysutils_systemd_unit`](./systemd_unit.md#unit-files-as-attributes), with one more section, `scope`, for `[Scope]` of scope units. The section of the unit's type must match `unit_name`: `service` for `ssh.service` or `service`, `scope` for `session-.scope`.

Drop-ins add to the unit's settings: a list directive such as `Environment=` or `After=` adds to the unit's own values, and a single-valued directive such as `User=` replaces the unit's value. To replace a list, start it with an empty string, which writes an empty assignment that clears the unit's values first, as in `exec_start = ["", "/usr/bin/new-command"]`. A service can only have one `ExecStart=` (unless it is `Type=oneshot`), so overriding the command always needs the empty assignment.

## Which Units a Drop-in Applies To

`unit_name` selects the directory `/etc/systemd/system/<unit_name>.d`:

| `unit_name` | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `nginx.service` | That unit. |
| `getty@.service` | Every instance of the template, such as `getty@tty1.service`. |
| `getty@tty1.service` | That instance only. Its drop-ins are applied after those of the template. |
| `user-.slice`, `session-.scope` | Every unit whose name starts with the part before the dash, such as `user-1000.slice` (systemd 240 and later). |
| `service`, `scope`, ... | Every unit of that type. |

Within the drop-ins of a unit, systemd applies the files in the order of their names across all directories, so names with a numeric prefix such as `50-limits` make the order explicit.

## Behavior

### Create

1. The provider refuses to create the drop-in if its file already exists; import it instead.
2. The directory `<unit_name>.d` is created with mode `0755` if it is missing, and the file is written atomically with mode `0644`, owned by the user running Terraform.
3. `systemctl daemon-reload` runs. For a single unit, or a template through the instance `<template>@sysutils-load-check`, the provider then checks that systemd still loads the unit: a drop-in with a fatal error, such as a second `ExecStart=` for a simple service, fails the apply (load state `bad-setting` or `error`). A unit that does not exist yet is fine, so a drop-in can be written before the package that installs the unit.
4. If `restart_on_change` is `true` and the unit is a running service, socket, mount, automount, swap, timer or path unit, it is restarted with `systemctl try-restart`, so that the drop-in takes effect.

If a step after writing the file fails, the resource is still recorded in state, marked as tainted, so the next apply replaces it and destroy cleans it up.

### Update

When the file differs from the configuration, it is replaced atomically, keeping its mode `0644`, and systemd is reloaded and the unit checked and restarted as on create. Changes to comments, blank lines, whitespace or line continuations only reload systemd and never restart the unit. Changing only `restart_on_change` or `timeout` does not touch the file.

### Destroy

The file is removed, and the `<unit_name>.d` directory too if it is empty then. systemd is reloaded, and with `restart_on_change`, a running unit is restarted so that it runs without the drop-in. If something other than a regular file sits at the drop-in's path, destroy fails and leaves it in place.

## Drift Detection

On refresh the provider reads the drop-in. A changed file shows up as a diff of `content` and of the section attributes for every directive that changed, and the next apply rewrites it. If the file was deleted, the resource is removed from state and the next plan recreates it. The unit's own unit file and other drop-ins are not watched.

## Timeouts

Every `systemctl` invocation is limited by `timeout` (2 minutes by default) and killed when it expires, which fails the apply. `systemctl try-restart` waits for the unit to restart, so choose a `timeout` longer than the unit's own `TimeoutStartSec=`/`TimeoutStopSec=`.

## Import

An existing drop-in can be imported by `<unit_name>/<name>`, with or without the `.conf` suffix:

```shell
# By <unit_name>/<name>, for /etc/systemd/system/nginx.service.d/50-limits.conf.
terraform import sysutils_systemd_dropin.nginx_limits nginx.service/50-limits
```

After import, `content` holds the file's contents and the section attributes the file as systemd reads it. `restart_on_change` and `timeout` are set to their defaults.

## Caveats

- The resource requires root and a host running systemd as PID 1. It manages drop-ins of the system instance only, in `/etc/systemd/system`, not of user units or of `/run/systemd/system`.
- Drop-ins for prefixes or whole unit types never restart anything, and neither do drop-ins for templates, targets, slices, scopes and devices. Resource-control settings of slices and scopes, such as `MemoryMax=`, take effect at the reload; other changes take effect when the units are next started. Use the [`sysutils_service`](../actions/service.md) action to restart units explicitly.
- A drop-in for every unit of a type, such as `service`, applies to all units of the host, including systemd's own. Test it carefully.
- The drop-in's contents are stored in Terraform state. Don't put secrets in `Environment=` lines; use `EnvironmentFile=` or credentials instead.
